name: Arcturus Defense Solutions AR-7 'Mandate'
description:
The standard-issue assault rifle of Arcturus Defense Solutions' corporate security divisions, the AR-7 Mandate represents the baseline of modern military lethality. Chambered in 6.5mm caseless, the rifle feeds from a 40-round helical magazine and features an integrated BCI smart-link port that allows neural fire-control for sub-MOA accuracy at combat distances. The polymer-ceramic receiver shrugs off environmental abuse from arctic operations to equatorial humidity.

The Mandate earned its name from the corporate policy that made it the mandatory sidearm for all Arcturus ground personnel above E-3 clearance. Its ubiquity in corporate conflict zones has made it one of the most recognized weapons on GLMZ, and surplus units flood grey markets whenever Arcturus rotates inventory cycles. Street-modified Mandates with disabled IFF transponders are a common sight in freelancer arsenals.

Cultural significance runs deep — owning a Mandate signals either corporate affiliation or the connections to acquire military hardware. In the lower tiers, a clean Mandate commands respect and suspicion in equal measure.
specifications:
caliber: 6.5mm caseless
effective_range: 550m
rate_of_fire: 750 rpm (cyclic)
magazine_capacity: 40 rounds (helical)
weight: 3.4 kg
tactical_use: The AR-7 excels as a general-purpose combat rifle across all engagement distances inside 600 meters. Its BCI integration allows trained operators to achieve precision fire without traditional optics, while the caseless ammunition system eliminates extraction failures and reduces carried weight. Corporate fireteams rely on the Mandate as their backbone weapon, supplementing with specialist platforms as needed.
cultural_context: The Mandate is the face of corporate military power. Seeing a column of Arcturus security carrying AR-7s is a common sight in contested economic zones, and the weapon's silhouette has become shorthand for corporate enforcement in street art and propaganda. Surplus Mandates are prized on the grey market — a clean unit with working BCI link fetches Φ4,500 or more.
story_hooks: A shipment of 200 Mandates with disabled IFF transponders has gone missing from an Arcturus depot — someone inside is arming an insurgency.
A freelancer discovers their grey-market Mandate still has an active Arcturus tracking beacon embedded in the receiver.

physical_description.visual_profile: A sleek, modern assault rifle with aggressive angular geometry. The receiver tapers slightly toward the muzzle, giving it a predatory silhouette. The integrated BCI port creates a distinctive raised module along the upper receiver. Overall impression: corporate precision meets combat pragmatism — expensive, purposeful, and designed for sustained fire.
physical_description.dimensions: Overall length: 94 cm | Barrel length: 41 cm | Width at receiver: 6.2 cm | Height with BCI module: 8.1 cm
physical_description.weight_description: Balanced and surprisingly manageable at 3.4 kg — the polymer-ceramic construction keeps it light without feeling fragile. Hangs naturally in a two-handed grip, with weight distributed evenly between receiver and barrel.
physical_description.primary_material: Polymer-ceramic composite receiver with steel barrel and bolt carrier group. Helical magazine housing is reinforced thermoplastic.
physical_description.finish: Matte gunmetal grey with brushed steel accents on the barrel and bolt carrier. The polymer-ceramic receiver has a subtle pearlescent sheen under direct light, hinting at its advanced composite construction.
physical_description.color_scheme: Gunmetal grey primary | Steel grey barrel | Glossy black polymer furniture and grip | White/silver manufacturer markings
physical_description.grip_texture: Textured polymer grip with shallow horizontal ridges for positive purchase even in wet conditions. The ergonomic curve fits naturally into a palm.
distinctive_features: Raised BCI neural-link module integrated flush into the upper receiver — circular port with data contact pins visible
Helical magazine with transparent polymer body showing 6.5mm caseless rounds stacked in spiral pattern
Charging handle positioned ambidextrous, recessed flush when not in use
Rail-less upper receiver — aesthetic of streamlined minimalism
Three small LED indicator ports (power, safety, target-lock) near the BCI module
Caseless ammunition feed system visible through magazine well — no brass ejection port
Muzzle slightly flared with recoil mitigation vanes
Ferro-ceramic heat sink band wrapped around mid-barrel, barely visible beneath finish
physical_description.manufacturer_markings: "ARCTURUS DEFENSE SOLUTIONS" stamped in sans-serif block letters along the left side of the receiver. "AR-7 MANDATE" engraved above the magazine well. Serial number laser-etched into the polymer furniture. Small Arcturus corporate sigil (stylized A with crosshairs) printed near the charging handle.
physical_description.condition_typical: Field-maintained and well-used. Most combat Mandates show wear on the grip texture, minor scratches on the muzzle, and discoloration around the magazine well from repeated loading cycles. Operators tend to keep them clean — IFF transponder circuits require maintenance. Grey market units often have the BCI module gutted or disabled, leaving visible scarring where the port was sealed.
